facts.project_name: 92NY — Kaufmann Concert Hall, Hall of Mirrors & Weill Art Gallery Interior Renovation
facts.notes: Concept design estimate for a ~10,000 SF interior renovation of three specialty spaces in an operating cultural venue (1930 building). Concept design package expected end of October; estimate required at that time. No budget, package contents, schedule, or phasing information provided.

deliverables.name: Concept Design Estimate — Interior Renovation
deliverables.description: Concept design construction cost estimate for the interior renovation of the Kaufmann Concert Hall, Hall of Mirrors, and Weill Art Gallery, prepared from the end-of-October concept design package: demolition, architectural finishes, millwork and seating, theatrical/AV/acoustic and specialty lighting allowances, MEP and fire protection modifications, and identified allowances; one estimate review meeting; incorporation of one consolidated round of comments; final issue.
deliverables.source_language: provide a proposal for concept design cost estimating services and confirm your availability to prepare the estimate at the end of October

gaps.question: The contents of the concept design package (plans, narratives, finish intent, system descriptions) are not yet defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: What can be measured versus what must be carried as allowance depends on the package's level of development.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The package is assumed to include concept plans and an outline design narrative for each space; design intent not yet drawn will be captured through clearly identified allowances and communicated back for confirmation at the estimate review.
gaps.pricing_basis: Concept-level estimate in Uniformat on approximately 10,000 SF, allowance-based where the package is not yet developed

gaps.question: No target construction budget or order-of-magnitude value has been shared.
gaps.why_it_matters: A stated target lets the estimate be presented against the budget with variances identified.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The estimate will establish the concept budget from first principles and benchmarks; if a target budget exists, it will be shared at kickoff so variances can be identified.
gaps.pricing_basis: One baseline concept estimate; no budget-reconciliation exercise assumed

gaps.question: Whether theatrical systems, audiovisual, and acoustic treatments at the Kaufmann Concert Hall are part of the renovation scope, and who procures them, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: These systems can rival the architectural cost of a concert hall renovation and are often owner-procured.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Theatrical, AV, acoustic, and specialty lighting scope shown in the concept package is carried as identified allowances developed with the design team; vendor-designed systems are priced as allowances only.
gaps.pricing_basis: Identified allowances per system, based on the package and design team input

gaps.question: Whether concert hall seating replacement and loose furnishings are in the renovation scope is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Seating is a major line in any concert hall renovation; loose FF&E is commonly owner-procured.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Fixed seating is priced as an allowance if shown in the concept package; loose furniture, fixtures and equipment, and artwork are excluded.
gaps.pricing_basis: Fixed-seating allowance per the package; loose FF&E and artwork excluded

gaps.question: The extent of restoration versus replacement of the historic and ornate finishes (notably the Hall of Mirrors) is not defined at concept stage.
gaps.why_it_matters: Restoration of decorative finishes carries specialty-trade premiums that dwarf standard fit-out rates.
gaps.proposed_assumption: Restoration scope is priced as identified allowances per the concept package's stated intent; no Landmarks Preservation Commission requirements are assumed unless identified in the package.
gaps.pricing_basis: Specialty restoration allowances per space; no LPC filings or requirements assumed

gaps.question: Whether mechanical, electrical, and fire protection work extends beyond the renovated spaces (e.g., plant or riser upgrades) is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Central plant or infrastructure work would materially change the estimate's scope.
gaps.proposed_assumption: MEP and fire protection work is limited to modifications within the ~10,000 SF renovation footprint; no central plant, service, or riser upgrades are assumed.
gaps.pricing_basis: MEP modifications within the renovation footprint only

gaps.question: Construction phasing around 92NY's performance and program calendar is not defined.
gaps.why_it_matters: Work around an active venue calendar forces off-hours labor and compressed-schedule premiums.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The building is assumed to remain in operation; an off-hours / occupied-venue work premium and logistics allowance is carried as a percentage on affected trades, with phasing to be developed with the project team.
gaps.pricing_basis: Percentage premium and logistics allowance on affected trades

gaps.question: No hazardous materials survey has been provided for spaces of this vintage.
gaps.why_it_matters: Abatement can materially affect demolition costs in a 1930s building.
gaps.proposed_assumption: An abatement allowance is carried as a separately identified line; hazardous materials survey and abatement design are excluded.
gaps.pricing_basis: Identified abatement allowance only, quantity unverified

gaps.question: Whether any structural modifications or elevator/lift work is contemplated is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Either would add scope well beyond an interior fit-out basis.
gaps.proposed_assumption: No structural modifications or vertical transportation work is assumed unless shown in the concept package.
gaps.pricing_basis: Interior fit-out basis; structure and VT excluded unless drawn

gaps.question: The anticipated construction start and duration are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Escalation to the construction midpoint needs a schedule basis.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The estimate is prepared in current-day dollars with escalation shown as a separately identified line to an assumed construction midpoint approximately 12 months from estimate issue.
gaps.pricing_basis: Escalation percentage applied as an identified line on the estimate summary

gaps.question: The concept package is expected at the end of October; the required turnaround is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The fee assumes a normal working turnaround, not an expedited one.
gaps.proposed_assumption: The draft estimate will be issued within two weeks of receipt of a complete concept package, with the final estimate issued within one week of receiving consolidated comments; expedited turnaround can be discussed if required.
gaps.pricing_basis: Draft in 2 weeks from complete package; final 1 week after comments

gaps.question: The review meeting format and number of comment rounds are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Each additional revision cycle adds assembly and review hours.
gaps.proposed_assumption: One estimate review meeting is included, held virtually; one consolidated round of review comments is incorporated in the final issue. Further meetings, revisions, or re-issues will be billed at the hourly rates herein.
gaps.pricing_basis: One virtual review meeting and one revision cycle included

exclusions_suggested: Loose furniture, fixtures & equipment (FF&E) and artwork
Theatrical, AV, and acoustic system design or procurement support (systems priced as allowances only)
Life cycle cost analysis / OPEX costing
Additional estimates or milestones beyond those listed above
Hazardous materials survey and abatement design
Reimbursables (to be billed at cost with no markup, if incurred)
